name: The Albanach
description: The Albanach takes its Gaelic name - meaning 'Scottish' or 'Highlander' - seriously, stocking over 330 different malt whiskies behind its High Street bar. Behind the pub's stone-walled front room, a quieter restaurant serves modern Scottish food, giving the building a split identity: buzzing whisky bar facing the Royal Mile, calmer dining room tucked away from it.
interesting_fact: With well over 300 malts on the shelf, the Albanach's whisky list is one of the largest on the entire Royal Mile - a serious collection for a street already packed with whisky bars.

name: The Advocate
description: The Advocate sits on Hunter Square right beside St Giles' Cathedral, converted into a pub in the 1990s in a building that takes its name from the legal profession clustered nearby around Parliament House. It reopened after a refit in May 2025, and still draws a daytime crowd of lawyers on their lunch break alongside the usual Old Town foot traffic.
interesting_fact: The pub can seat over 200 people and runs live music through the week - acoustic sets on Sunday nights, livelier entertainment on Fridays - a scale that's easy to miss from its fairly modest Hunter Square frontage.
source_notes: Ad hoc backlog batch 2026-09-02. Distinct from the existing 'Advocate's Close' POI (leg 6) - checked, not a duplicate.

name: Malt Shovel Inn
description: The Malt Shovel occupies a building dating to around 1800 on Cockburn Street, a curving Victorian street cut through the Old Town in the 1850s specifically to give better carriage access up to the newly built Waverley Station. Inside, the pub keeps its period character - corniced ceilings, dark woodwork, and stained glass - across three connected rooms.
interesting_fact: Cockburn Street itself is a rare piece of deliberate town planning slotted into the organic, centuries-old street pattern of the Old Town - built purely to solve a 19th-century traffic problem.

name: The Piper's Rest
description: The Piper's Rest sits on Hunter Square just behind the Tron Kirk, serving Scottish food - haggis, Cullen skink, steak pie - alongside a solid range of malt whiskies, local gins, and craft beers. Live music runs seven nights a week, mixing traditional Scottish tunes with more contemporary covers.
interesting_fact: The pub's golden bagpiper figures displayed in its window cases give it one of the more eye-catching frontages on Hunter Square, visible from the top of the square day or night.
